messages.content: "你能告訴我著名足球運動員莱萊納爾·梅西的淨資產是多少歐元嗎？之後，我想知道籃球運動員勒布朗·詹姆斯的淨資產是多少英鎊。此外，我對一個使用公制系統的重85公斤、身高180公分的人的身體質量指數（BMI）也很好奇。最後，你能計算一個使用英制系統的重200磅、身高6英呎2英吋的人的BMI嗎？"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

We have functions: celebrity_net_worth_get(name, currency). For Messi, name "Lionel Messi" presumably. Currency: "EUR". For LeBron James, name "LeBron James", currency: "GBP". Then BMI calculation: calculate_bmi(weight, height, unit). For metric: weight 85, height 180, unit "metric". For imperial: weight 200 lbs, height 6'2" -> need convert to pounds? The function expects weight in kilograms if unit metric, or pounds if unit imperial? The description: weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. Optional unit 'imperial' or 'metric'. So if unit imperial, weight should be in pounds, height in inches? But description says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. That seems contradictory. But likely if unit imperial, weight in pounds, height in inches. So we need to pass weight 200, height 74 inches (6*12+2). unit "imperial". Then function returns BMI. We'll call functions twice for BMI. Then output results. Use function calls.
